So I have a 10g betta tank with black gravel and a hut thing and some amazon sword, a couple of moss balls and a bit of drift wood. My fighter has explored his tank and appears to be bored with it. I want to add some of my gemstones to the tank to give him something to think about but am unsure with how they will react with the water. One of them is an amethyst crystal, will this react with water? I also have some tigers eye too.

If not, can anyone suggest a cheap but glittery gem stone ornaments? Ideally small enough to swap around every now and then to change the scenery for him every month or two.
Natural gemstones and crystals for my tank"

I don't think gemstones would have any effect on the water at all! If they did, it'd more than likely be very little, and if your concerned about it you could just test the water before and after. I think the most it'd do would alter the PH very slightly, if anything! Also if you were going to add a whole bunch, but I think you're fine with a few pieces!

Maybe you could get him some sort of small tank mate? I know White Clouds can be with Bettas, Ember Tetras, and some other small fish. Maybe some Ghost Shrimp and let him hunt them down? If anything it would give him something to do or look forward to in terms of a treat!

Hes in there with 5 minnows and 3 corys. And mineral crystals are fine (after doing some research) as long as they don't contain dissolvable minerals or metals in them. So amethyst which is just coloured quartz is fine :P which is what I put in and it looks great. Thought stuff like pyrite is really bad as it has heavy metals which can kill a fish! So quartz/silica based minerals are good :)
Ahh, well that's good then! Glad everything worked out! :)

I'm happy to announce that we now have flairs!

I decided to try something else than just deleting things. Instead of deleting borderline stuff, I'll for now add a flair to them.

Important note: The rules as stated in the sidebar are still in effect. Violating these still trigger a delete.

Also Rule 4 will be added. It states that submissions must be accessible from everywhere globally. Explicit exception to this rule are censor filters implemented by companies or local governments. Those affected may have our sympathy. This rule will be added once saving the text doesn't error out

Available flairs

  • No flair – For anything that there's no real flair for?
  • Meta – Meta discussions
  • OT – For off-topic stuff. Somewhat programming related, but then not really.
  • Security – Stuff that's security related, security patches, advisories, "Don't store passwords as plaintext" kind of articles, etc.
  • Help – For when people are seeking help on a programming related issue, how to get into it, that kind of stuff
  • Microsoft/Linux/Apple – For submissions specific to products by MS or Apple, or specific to Linux based operating systems. I haven't seen yet a BSD specific, so ...
  • Opinion – Submissions that are less objective and more opinionated towards something.
  • Educational –- Submissions that are generally educational
  • Beginner – Submissions targeted at beginners in general or for something specific. A tutorial for a first project in some framework or basic knowledge find their place here.
